title: J.D. Roberts: OU Guard Who Won the 1953 Outland Trophy
question: Which Oklahoma guard won the Outland Trophy in 1953?
answer: J.D. Roberts, a two-way guard for Bud Wilkinson, won the 1953 Outland Trophy as the nation's top interior lineman. He was a consensus All-American that season and later became head coach of the New Orleans Saints.
summary: J.D. Roberts won the 1953 Outland Trophy as a two-way guard at Oklahoma, helped start the 47-game streak, and later coached the New Orleans Saints in the NFL.
body: J.D. Roberts did not look like a typical lineman. The National Football Foundation lists him at just 5-foot-10 and 210 pounds, yet in 1953 he was voted the best interior lineman in the country, bringing the Outland Trophy to Norman for the second time in three years.

Roberts played right guard on offense in 1951 and 1952, then became a two-way player as a senior. That season he was a consensus All-American and collected Lineman of the Year recognition from several outlets, including the AP and UP. OU's history page describes him as so rugged and aggressive that he was difficult to block. One of his blocked punts set up a win over Colorado.

His 1953 team went 9-1-1, beat No. 1 Maryland in the Orange Bowl and finished fourth in the final rankings. It also got a historic run started: the Sooners' 19-14 win over Texas on Oct. 10, 1953, was the first victory of what became the record 47-game winning streak.

The Green Bay Packers took Roberts in the 17th round of the 1954 draft, but he never played a regular-season NFL game. He served as a second lieutenant in the Marine Corps, then turned to coaching, with assistant jobs at Denver, Houston, Navy, Auburn and Oklahoma. He was on the original New Orleans Saints staff and was named the Saints' interim head coach on Nov. 3, 1970. His first game in charge was a 19-17 win over Detroit, sealed by Tom Dempsey's then-record 63-yard field goal.
Roberts entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 1993 and later ran an oil and gas business in Oklahoma City. He died in May 2021 at age 88.
